title: PV production is read with no age check: a silent or future-stamped meter still seeds step 0 and is published
claim: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._pv_measured_production reads CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY through hass.states.get + state_power_kw, never through InputReader, so the 30-minute limit const.INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY] declares is never applied: in 6 of 6 report ages past the limit (31 min to 24 h) and for a report stamped 90 min in the future, the real cycle publishes data['pv']['measured_production_kw']=5.0 and overwrites step 0 of the PV forecast with it.
mechanism: _pv_forecast sets production[0] = min(self._pv_production, peak_kw) from _pv_measured_production, which is `state_power_kw(self.hass.states.get(entity_id), sign='clamp')`. state_power_kw's own docstring calls itself 'the one parse of a power state outside InputReader (which adds the staleness of a configured input)'; the slot has a declared limit (const.py: INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY] = 30.0, INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES pv_production_entity 30.0) that no reader of it applies, and the slot never appears in the input watchdog (staleness.py: 'unread'). An inverter whose integration drops off mid-afternoon keeps the planner believing in its last output (here 5 kW) for the current step indefinitely, and a host clock stepped back makes the same reading look fresh.

evidence.unit: report ages past the 30-min limit (of 6) at which the stale reading is published and used; plus future_published=1
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

perturbation.change: --fix: _pv_measured_production first reads the slot through InputReader(hass, {}).read(CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY, entity_id=...) and returns None unless the reading is ok (the declared age limit applies), then state_power_kw as before; patched in memory
perturbation.observed_value: stale_cells_published=0, future_published=0; ages 5 and 20 min still publish 5.0

metric_definition: Of 6 report ages beyond INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[pv_production] (31,45,90,180,420,1440 min), how many cycles still publish pv.measured_production_kw from the stale state.
phenomenon_property: Every configured input with a declared age limit is read under that limit by every consumer; a reading past its limit (or stamped ahead of the clock) is not used as a measurement and not published as one.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/consumers.py  (per d1-inputs slot, the production functions calling hass.states.get on it; a slot listed in const.INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES whose getters bypass InputReader/age_of is a seam)

null_control.note: the same cells with the meter re-reporting at each cycle: the reading is legitimately used, no stale cell counted

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py:_pv_measured_production reads through InputReader (age_limit_for) so the declared 30-min limit and the future-stamp refusal apply; the slot then shows in the input watchdog.
